title: Use and care for tools and equipment

lessons.title: Choosing the right tool
lessons.html:
Tools and equipment at work

In an abattoir or meat plant you use many tools: knives, steels, saws, hooks, scabbards, scales, hoses, trolleys and cleaning brushes. Using the right tool for the job keeps you safe, protects the meat and saves time.

Common tools and what they are for

ToolUse
Boning knifeRemoving meat from bones
Sticking knifeBleeding after stunning
SteelKeeping the knife edge straight and sharp during work
Sharpening stonePutting a new edge on a blunt knife
Brisket or carcass sawCutting through bone
Meat hookHolding and moving meat safely
ScabbardHolding your knife safely on your belt

Check before you use

  • Is it the correct tool for this job?
  • Is it clean and sterilised?
  • Is the handle firm and not cracked?
  • Is the blade sharp and not chipped?
  • For power tools, are guards in place and is the cable or hose undamaged?

If a tool is damaged, do not use it. Tag it and give it to your supervisor. A chipped knife can leave a metal piece in the meat. A cracked handle can let your hand slip onto the blade.

Your own protection

Wear the protective clothing your job needs: a mesh glove on the hand that holds the meat, a mesh apron if required, boots with good grip, and hearing protection near saws. PPE does not replace safe work, but it reduces injury when something goes wrong.

lessons.title: Using tools safely
lessons.html:
Safe ways of working

Knife safety

  • Always cut away from your body.
  • Keep your other hand out of the line of the cut.
  • Keep your knife sharp. A blunt knife needs more force and slips more easily.
  • Keep the knife in the scabbard when walking. Never carry an open knife.
  • Never try to catch a falling knife. Step back and let it fall.
  • Do not leave knives in sinks or under meat where someone cannot see them.
  • Never use a knife to open boxes or as a screwdriver.

Using a steel

Hold the steel firmly, away from your body. Draw the knife down the steel at a small angle, one side and then the other, a few times. Your trainer will show you the correct angle. Keep your fingers behind the guard.

Saws and power tools

  • Only use a power tool if you have been trained and authorised.
  • Check the guard before starting.
  • Keep both hands on the handles.
  • Never remove guards or block safety switches.
  • Switch off and wait for the blade to stop before putting it down.
  • Switch off and isolate before cleaning or changing blades.

Hooks, trolleys and lifting equipment

Hang meat on hooks firmly. Push trolleys and rail hooks, do not pull them towards you. Watch for people in your path. Do not overload trolleys and never stand under a load on a hoist.

Hygiene while working

Sterilise knives and tools in the steriliser between carcasses and whenever they touch a dirty surface, the floor or the hide. If a tool falls on the floor, it must be cleaned and sterilised before you use it again.

lessons.title: Cleaning, storing and maintaining tools
lessons.html:
Looking after tools

Tools that are cared for last longer, work better and are safer.

Cleaning after use

  1. Remove meat, fat and blood with a brush and water.
  2. Wash with the approved detergent.
  3. Rinse with clean water.
  4. Sterilise in hot water or use the approved sanitiser, following the plant procedure.
  5. Let tools dry on a clean rack.

Wear gloves and eye protection when using cleaning chemicals. Never mix chemicals.

Storing tools

  • Store knives in a knife rack, box or scabbard, with blades covered.
  • Keep tools in their marked place so they can be found and counted.
  • Store power tools in a dry place with cables neatly rolled.
  • Do not leave tools on the floor or on top of machines.

Sharpening and maintenance

Use the steel often during the shift to keep the edge. When the knife becomes blunt, sharpen it on a stone or take it to the person responsible for sharpening. Saws and power tools are maintained by trained maintenance staff. Report any problem, such as a strange noise, overheating or vibration, straight away.

Counting tools

Many plants check that all tools are present at the start and end of the shift. A missing knife or blade piece could be in the product. If a tool or part is missing, tell your supervisor immediately.

Reporting damage

Report damaged tools, do not hide them. Fill in the tool register or tell your supervisor so the tool can be repaired or replaced.

Key points

  • Choose the correct tool and check it before use.
  • Cut away from your body and keep your knife in the scabbard when walking.
  • Never catch a falling knife.
  • Only use power tools if trained, with guards in place.
  • Clean, sterilise and store tools in their correct place.
  • Report damaged or missing tools immediately.
